newsitem.title: CANADA: Federated gives final okay to Canada pipe project.
newsitem.headline: Federated gives final okay to Canada pipe project.

text.p: Federated Pipe Lines Ltd said on Tuesday it would award the remaining construction contracts for a C$106 million oil and natural gas liquids pipeline expansion in northeastern British Columbia and northwestern Alberta.

When built, the lines will gather oil, propane plus, ethane plus and segregated condensate at Taylor, British Columbia and Dunvegan, Alberta and transport the volumes to Judy Creek, Fort Saskatchewan and Edmonton, Alberta by the spring of 1998. Federated is co-owned by Anderson Exploration Ltd and Imperial Oil Ltd.
Federated said 90 percent of the system's capacity was committed in an open season for potential shippers.
It said the capital cost of the project was the largest single investment in the company's 40-year history and C$25 million for purchases had been committed to date.

"The significant level of producer support for the pipelines...demonstrates the desire of the producing industry for the services offered by Federated and 'in-the-ground' competition," Federated President Larry Macdonald said in a statement.
Construction was slated to start in June.
